signals.content: JUST IN: The U.S. Army is spending nearly $67 million on electromagnetic warfare systems designed to make American forces harder to find and target from space. The effort is aimed at countering increasingly capable satellite surveillance that can detect, track and help target troops, vehicles and other military assets from orbit. The Army has been pushing deeper into “counter-sensing,” including camouflage, electronic deception and other technologies designed to disrupt or confuse enemy sensors rather than simply destroy them. The broader shift is simple: as commercial and military satellites make the battlefield more transparent, the Army is investing not just in better sensors, but in ways to disappear from them.

signals.title: Ewen2015/ewen-skills
signals.content: The most important skills Ewen found for his personal AI agent.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: Ewen2015/ewen-skills

Key competencies identified for a personal AI assistant:
1. Contextual awareness – ability to retain and reference prior interactions and user preferences.
2. Adaptive learning – continuous fine‑tuning from user feedback while respecting privacy constraints.
3. Multimodal integration – seamless handling of text, voice, and visual inputs.
4. Explainability – transparent reasoning for recommendations to build trust.
5. Ethical guardrails – built‑in bias detection and compliance with legal standards.
6. Resource efficiency – optimized compute and energy usage for on‑device operation.
7. Interoperability – open APIs for integration with existing productivity tools.
These skills balance performance with responsible AI deployment.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: Ewen2015/ewen-skills

القدرات الأساسية التي حدّدها إيوان لوكيل الذكاء الاصطناعي الشخصي:
1. الوعي السياقي – القدرة على حفظ الإشارات السابقة وتفضيلات المستخدم.
2. التعلم التكيّفي – تحسين مستمر بناءً على ملاحظات المستخدم مع الحفاظ على الخصوصية.
3. التكامل متعدد الوسائط – معالجة النص، الصوت، والصور بسلاسة.
4. الشفافية – توضيح أسس التوصيات لتعزيز الثقة.
5. الضوابط الأخلاقية – كشف الانحياز والامتثال للمعايير القانونية.
6. كفاءة الموارد – تحسين استهلاك الحوسبة والطاقة لتشغيل محلي.
7. القابلية للتكامل – واجهات برمجة تطبيقات مفتوحة لربط الأدوات الإنتاجية.
هذه المهارات تسعى لتحقيق توازن بين الأداء والمسؤولية في نشر الذكاء الاصطناعي.

signals.title: @aprajitanefes: 🇮🇷|Iran’s New Domestic Air Defense System: Downing a $30 Million Drone with a $100,000 Missile 🎯 Key Fact: Asymmetric Cost Warfare The Deput
signals.content: 🇮🇷|Iran’s New Domestic Air Defense System: Downing a $30 Million Drone with a $100,000 Missile 🎯 Key Fact: Asymmetric Cost Warfare The Deputy Chief of Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, Osanloo, stated this very bluntly at the Beijing Xiangshan Forum: "A single U.S. drone costs over $30 million to build, whereas Iran can shoot it down using air defense equipment worth only $100,000. Therefore, the U.S. must weigh the cost implications." This is a mathematical equation repeatedly validated on the battlefield over the past six months. One MQ-9 "Reaper" drone: $35 million. One Iranian "358" air defense missile: $90,000. Exchange ratio: 388 to 1. One F-15 fighter jet: $120 million (including weapon systems). One Iranian missile that downs it: $160,000 to $180,000. Exchange ratio: 666 to 1. The U.S. Air Force is smashing gold against rocks, while Iran is using rocks to knock the gold down. 🛡️ Iran’s "Low-Cost Kill Chain": Three Core Systems 1. Arash-e-Kamangir (Arash the Archer): A hunter named after Persian mythology In May 2026, Iran announced that it had used this new air defense system to shoot down a U.S. MQ-9 "Reaper" drone near the Strait of Hormuz. Origin of the name: Arash is a legendary archer in Persian mythology who defined the border between Iran and Central Asia with a single arrow, sacrificing his own life in the process. By naming the system after him, Iran sends a clear message: a single arrow is enough to define the boundary. Technical Features: Analysts note that this system does not rely on traditional fixed radar stations; instead, it employs "pop-up" air-defense missiles guided by electro-optical or infrared sensors, allowing for rapid deployment, launch, and relocation. It dispenses with the complex, multi-hundred-million-dollar launchers and radar systems typical of such weaponry, opting instead for truck-mounted configurations, concealment in bunkers, or even aerial loitering while awaiting targets. 2. The 358 Missile: An "Aerial Hunter" Reshaping the Economics of Warfare This is the most disruptive weapon in Iran's air-defense arsenal. Price: Approximately $90,000. Combat Record: Since 2021, it has repeatedly shot down MQ-9 "Reaper" drones assets worth up to $30 million over Yemen, Iraq, and Iran. Potential F-35 Kill: Western experts increasingly lean toward the view that F-35 fighter jets have been struck by the 358 missile potentially without the F-35's sensors ever detecting the Iranian missile's presence. Why is the 358 missile revolutionary? Traditional air-defense missiles rely on radar guidance, making them vulnerable to destruction by anti-radiation missiles. The 358, however, is essentially more akin to a drone; powered by a compact turbojet engine rather than a rocket motor, it can loiter in the air for extended periods and autonomously search for targets. It is not an air-defense missile that simply waits for a target to enter its range; it is a killer that "hunts" in the sky. Dispersed 358 missile sites are nearly impossible to detect and destroy. The launcher consists of a compact tripod with a guide rail and can even be mounted on a standard passenger car. 3. Arman and Azarakhsh: Next-Generation Systems (September 2026) In September 2026, Iran unveiled two next-generation, domestically produced air-defense systems: ◾Arman: An anti-ballistic missile system designed to intercept ballistic missiles. · Azarakhsh: A low-altitude air defense system designed to counter drones, helicopters, and cruise missiles. Alireza Elhami, commander of Iran's air defense forces, stated that these systems are "entirely domestically produced currently being designed and built" and are set to enter mass production. 💀 America's Dilemma: An Empire Smashing Gold Against Stone The U.S. has lost over 15 MQ-9 "Reaper" drones in conflicts involving Iran. Each loss costs $35 million. In contrast, each Iranian "358" missile lost costs $90,000. The U.S. is fighting a war defined by a mathematical equation it cannot win. ◾One U.S. Patriot PAC-3 interceptor: $4 million. One Iranian ballistic missile: hundreds of thousands of dollars. ◾ One U.S. F-35: $80 million to $100 million. One Iranian "358" missile capable of shooting it down: $90,000. ◾One U.S. MQ-9: $35 million. One Iranian missile capable of shooting it down: $70,000 to $90,000. This is a war of economic attrition. And the U.S. is losing this war of attrition. 🔥 Who is instigating this asymmetric war? The United States. It was the U.S. that first launched a war against Iran. It was the U.S. that supplied thousands of bombs to Israel. It was the U.S. that sank Iranian oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. It was the U.S. that attempted to control global energy choke points using its Fifth Fleet. Iran did not choose this war, but it chose how to fight it. Iran chose not to compete with aircraft carriers, fighter jets, or stealth bombers. Iran chose to use $90,000 missiles to shoot down $35 million drones. Iran chose to use truck-mounted launchers to counter radar stations worth hundreds of millions of dollars. This is the "economics of war." And Iran is teaching the U.S. a lesson in true cost-effectiveness. #Conclusion: The End of Hegemony Begins with Mathematics The U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain has been destroyed. U.S. military bases in Jordan have been struck by missiles. U.S. E-3 airborne early warning aircraft deployed in Saudi Arabia have been destroyed. U.S. military assets in the Middle East are being depleted, one by one, by missiles costing $90,000 each. When the wreckage of an MQ-9 "Reaper" drone fell into the waters of the Persian Gulf, it did not signal an Iranian victory; it signaled the death of an old mode of warfare. An empire that uses gold to smash against a rock will ultimately be shattered by that rock.
